title: Omega-Fold Constructibility: Existential Closure
content: Defines IsOmegaFoldConstructible as the existential closure over all fold levels: a degree d is omega-fold constructible if there exists some k such that d is k-fold constructible. This collapses the infinite tower of fold hierarchies (1-fold, 2-fold, 3-fold, ...) into a single predicate. The key insight is that we don't ask 'which level works?' but only 'does some level work?'
mathContext: $\text{IsOmegaFoldConstructible}(d) :\!\!\iff \exists k \in \mathbb{N},\; \text{IsKFoldConstructible}(d, k)$. This is the set-theoretic union $\bigcup_{k=0}^{\infty} \mathcal{C}_k$ where $\mathcal{C}_k$ is the class of $k$-fold constructible degrees.

title: Monotonicity: k-Fold Implies Omega-Fold
content: Two foundational lemmas establish the relationship between finite and omega-fold constructibility. omega_fold_one shows degree 1 is omega-fold constructible (trivially, using any k ≥ 1). omega_fold_of_kfold is the monotonicity witness: k-fold constructibility implies omega-fold constructibility, proved by simply exhibiting the witness k. These appear trivial but are needed to close reasoning chains that go through finite levels.
mathContext: $\text{IsKFoldConstructible}(d, k) \implies \text{IsOmegaFoldConstructible}(d)$ for any $k$. Equivalently: $\mathcal{C}_k \subseteq \mathcal{C}_{\omega}$ for all $k \in \mathbb{N}$.

title: kfold_self: Bertrand's Postulate Powers the Key Bound
content: The central computational lemma: every positive degree d is d-fold constructible. The proof uses foldPrimeBound(d) = p_{d+1} (the (d+1)-th prime), and crucially that p_{d+1} ≥ d+2. Since any prime factor q of d satisfies q ≤ d < d+2 ≤ p_{d+1} = foldPrimeBound(d), all prime factors of d are below the fold bound. The bound p_n ≥ n+2 is a weak form of Bertrand's Postulate (there exists a prime between n and 2n), available in Mathlib as Nat.add_two_le_nth_prime.
mathContext: $\text{IsKFoldConstructible}(d, d)$ for all $d \geq 1$. Key inequality: if $q \mid d$ and $q$ prime, then $q \leq d < d+2 \leq p_{d+1} = \text{foldPrimeBound}(d)$. Uses $p_n \geq n+2$ (from Bertrand) where $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime (0-indexed).

title: Degree 0 Fails: Positivity is a Definitional Barrier
content: The theorem not_omega_fold_zero shows degree 0 cannot be omega-fold constructible. The proof is immediate: if degree 0 were k-fold constructible for some k, the IsKFoldConstructible definition requires a positivity witness hpos : 0 > 0, which is a contradiction. This is not a deep mathematical obstruction — it is a deliberate definitional choice that degree 0 is excluded (there is no polynomial equation of degree 0 to 'solve'). The proof pattern `intro ⟨k, _, hpos, _⟩; omega` extracts the positivity field and derives False.
mathContext: $\neg\, \text{IsOmegaFoldConstructible}(0)$ because $\text{IsKFoldConstructible}(0, k)$ requires $0 > 0$, which is false. The IsSmooth predicate (and hence IsKFoldConstructible) enforces $d > 0$ as a precondition.

title: Main Theorem: Algebraic Completeness via Sharp Biconditional
content: omega_fold_complete_iff is the principal result: omega-fold origami is algebraically complete if and only if the degree is positive. The proof is a two-direction biconditional. Forward direction (→): any witness k for IsKFoldConstructible d k comes with a positivity field, so d > 0. Backward direction (←): if d > 0, apply omega_fold_pos (which applies kfold_self with witness k = d). The result is a sharp characterization — not just 'omega-fold is powerful' but 'omega-fold captures exactly the positive degrees, and the exception is precisely degree 0.'
mathContext: $\text{IsOmegaFoldConstructible}(d) \iff d > 0$. Equivalently, $\mathcal{C}_{\omega} = \mathbb{N}_{>0}$: the omega-fold constructible degrees are exactly the positive natural numbers.

title: Monotone Growth: All Sufficiently Large Fold Levels Work
content: eventually_all_folds_sufficient proves that for any positive degree d, every fold level k ≥ d is sufficient. This is the 'eventually' direction: once you have enough folds, adding more doesn't hurt. The proof re-uses the core inequality: since q ≤ d ≤ k, we have q < d+2 ≤ k+2 ≤ foldPrimeBound(k), so the fold bound at level k dominates any prime factor of d. This establishes the upward closure of the fold hierarchy — IsKFoldConstructible is monotone in k.
mathContext: $\forall d > 0,\, \forall k \geq d: \text{IsKFoldConstructible}(d, k)$. Proof: $q \mid d$ prime $\Rightarrow q \leq d \leq k \Rightarrow q < k+2 \leq p_{k+1} = \text{foldPrimeBound}(k)$.

title: Explicit Fold Bound: d Folds Always Suffice for Degree d
content: min_folds_finite packages kfold_self into a concrete existence statement: for every positive degree d, there exists a minimum fold level k_min ≤ d that constructs d, and d itself works. This gives an explicit and computable upper bound on the fold complexity function min_k(d). The proof is one line: exhibit k_min = d and invoke kfold_self.
mathContext: $\forall d > 0,\, \exists k_{\min} \leq d:\; \text{IsKFoldConstructible}(d, k_{\min})$. The bound $k_{\min} \leq d$ is tight for prime $d = p_m$: the minimum fold level is exactly $m-1$ (the prime's index), which may be much smaller than $d$.

title: Prime Fold Thresholds: Exact Characterization for Primes
content: prime_kfold_iff_bound gives the exact fold threshold for prime degrees: a prime p is k-fold constructible if and only if p ≤ foldPrimeBound(k) = p_{k+1}. For primes, there are no composite factors to worry about — p only divides itself, so the IsSmooth condition reduces to checking p against the bound. The forward direction extracts the bound from the smooth condition applied to p (which divides p). The reverse direction uses hp.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd to eliminate q = 1. This means the fold threshold for prime p is exactly its prime index: p = p_m requires fold level ≥ m-1.
mathContext: For prime $p$ and $k \geq 1$: $\text{IsKFoldConstructible}(p, k) \iff p \leq p_{k+1}$. Equivalently, $\text{min\_fold}(p_m) = m-1$ where $p_m$ is the $m$-th prime. Example: $\text{min\_fold}(11) = \text{min\_fold}(p_5) = 4$.

title: Concrete Instances: Classic Problems Are Omega-Fold Constructible
content: Six concrete instances ground the abstract theorem in familiar mathematics. Degree 3 corresponds to angle trisection and cube root of 2 — impossible by ruler-and-compass but solvable by single-fold origami. Degree 5 is the quintic, whose general non-solvability (Abel-Ruffini) is a separate statement — here it just means the quintic CAN be solved geometrically via origami. Degree 11 marks the transition from 3-fold to 4-fold origami. Degree 100 shows the bound is not a theoretical curiosity: 100 simultaneous folds suffice for any 100th-degree polynomial. omega_fold_zero_unique_failure packages all cases: ¬ IsOmegaFoldConstructible d ↔ d = 0.
mathContext: Specializations of $\text{IsOmegaFoldConstructible}(d) \iff d > 0$: $d \in \{2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 100\}$ all satisfy $d > 0$. The companion theorem $\forall d:\; \neg\,\text{IsOmegaFoldConstructible}(d) \iff d = 0$ says degree 0 is the UNIQUE failure.

title: Omega-Fold as Union: Structural Clarity Theorems
content: The final section restates the relationship between finite and omega-fold constructibility in two equivalent forms. kfold_le_omega is the inclusion witness (same as omega_fold_of_kfold, restated for clarity). omega_fold_as_union is the definitional unfolding: IsOmegaFoldConstructible d ↔ ∃ k, IsKFoldConstructible d k — proved by Iff.rfl since the definition is literally this existential. Together these form a clean summary: the omega level is the colimit (direct limit) of the fold hierarchy, and membership in the colimit is exactly having a representative at some finite level.
mathContext: $\text{IsOmegaFoldConstructible}(d) \iff \exists k \in \mathbb{N},\; \text{IsKFoldConstructible}(d, k)$ — the omega level is the colimit of the diagram $\mathcal{C}_0 \subseteq \mathcal{C}_1 \subseteq \mathcal{C}_2 \subseteq \cdots$.
